questions: Should the function raise a ValueError if the DataFrame has columns but all values in the last column are NaN after dropping NaN values (i.e., effectively no data to compute skewness)?
Is the skewness calculation expected to use bias correction (e.g., scipy.stats.skew's default bias=True) or should it be unbiased (bias=False)?
Should the function handle cases where the last column is of non-numeric type (e.g., strings) by raising an error or attempting conversion?
If the DataFrame has only one column, is that column considered the 'last column' and thus used, or should it raise an error?
Should the function raise an error if the DataFrame has no columns (i.e., zero columns) as opposed to being empty (zero rows)?
Is the function expected to modify the input DataFrame (e.g., by dropping NaN values in-place) or leave it unchanged?
Should the function treat infinite values (inf or -inf) in the last column specially, e.g., by dropping them, raising an error, or passing them to skew?
Is the skewness calculation expected to be performed on the entire last column including duplicate column names, or should it handle duplicate column names uniquely?
